Subject: SLO measurement details + temporary exception for migration test

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups for our security and platform teams before we sign the PO: specifically we need detail on how Redwood measures uptime and latency SLOs, how alerts are generated, and whether our engineers can get short-term access to monitoring during the migration window.

Two asks:
- A short summary of the SLO definitions you use (availability window, measurement frequency, latency percentiles tied to SLOs).
- Confirmation on read-only dashboard access for our SREs and any constraints.

Separately, we are planning a large dataset migration next week that will temporarily increase load on the inference endpoints. Our SREs are asking whether Redwood can grant a temporary throughput/latency exception (72 hours) where you agree not to escalate SLA credits while we run load verification — we will coordinate exact windows. If an exception is possible, please outline the acceptance criteria and rollback triggers.

Can you get us something by EOD PT today? Procurement needs the text for internal approval.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, Globex Corporation

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: SLO measurement details + temporary exception for migration test

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and timeline. Below is a concise package you can drop into Procurement / Security. I’m attaching a PDF with the metric tables and a text file with the Grafana invite instructions.

SLO & measurement summary (TL;DR):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly availability for production inference endpoints. Measured as successful 200 responses / total requests in rolling 30-day windows.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 1.2s for standard model class (small-medium requests). For large context or GPU-heavy models we publish model-class-specific p95/p99 in the attached PDF.
- Measurement frequency: 1-minute buckets aggregated to 15m/1h windows for dashboards and 30-day rolling for SLA calculations.
- Error classification: 5xx and timeouts count as errors; client-aborts are excluded if caller-side dropped the TCP connection.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Primary telemetry: Grafana dashboards backed by Prometheus/Thanos (internal) + Datadog for synthetic checks.
- Alerting thresholds (examples): p99 latency > 1.5s for 5m triggers a Sev2 (pager) to our infra on-call; availability drop below 99.9% for 30m triggers SEV1.
- Alert routing: customer-impacting alerts route to on-call with automatic failover. Non-customer-impacting degradations are routed to engineering watchers.

Customer access:
- We provide read-only Grafana access scoped to the customer’s project and endpoints. Invite process: we send a one-time link (instructions attached: grafana-view-invite.txt). Role = read-only, no alert-management privileges.
- We can also provide synthetic-check logs and a curated set of query templates for your SREs.

Temporary exception request (proposed):
- Window: 2027-03-02 00:00 UTC -> 2027-03-05 23:59 UTC (72 hours).
- Scope: Exception limited to elevated p95/p99 during migration verification across the stated endpoints; availability goals remain intact unless we mutually agree to relax a specific endpoint.
- Acceptance criteria:
  * You provide expected traffic profile and cadence 72 hours before start.
  * We coordinate a runbook and a point-of-contact for automated rollback.
  * During the window, our on-call will classify incidents under the exception unless they meet an agreed severity threshold (data loss or authentication failures).
- Rollback triggers (we will rollback to deny traffic or divert to standby capacity): sustained p99 > 3.5s for 15m OR error rate > 2% sustained for 10m.
- Credits: Exception would mean we agree not to pursue SLA credit calculations for spikes within this window provided the above constraints are met.

Attachments: slo-metrics-breakdown.pdf (detailed tables), grafana-view-invite.txt (one-time access instructions). I’ve also attached the exception-request-form.docx for procurement to sign/ack.

If this looks good I’ll loop in karthik (ops lead) to sign-off on the rollback triggers and on-call staffing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
